regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 56.5","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY looks unimpeachable until you note that GVA growth typically trails by 100–150 bps and core sector at 4.8% YoY is decelerating even as IIP capital goods surges 16.9% YoY. The PMI Composite at 56.5 is services-led — manufacturing at 55.7 is solid but not the driver. The inversion: if capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is the honest signal, then the investment cycle is real; but core sector deceleration suggests the upstream materials economy hasn't caught up with the headline.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 6.09% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"CPI at 6.09% YoY is above the RBI's 6% tolerance ceiling for the first time in this cycle, driven by food at 8.94% YoY and fuel at 22.93% YoY — the latter at the 95th percentile of its 10-year range. Core CPI at 4.5% YoY is rising but not yet alarming. The dangerous gap: headline is being driven by supply-side shocks (fuel, food) that rate hikes cannot cure, yet the RBI's own inflation forecast has moved to 5.1% YoY — a forecast that already looks stale. If food inflation stays above 8% through Q4, the RBI's pause becomes politically untenable.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.54% YoY; CD ratio 82%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.54% YoY against deposit growth at 16.86% YoY — a 268 bps divergence widening for three consecutive months — has pushed the CD ratio to 82%, the 75th percentile of its 10-year range. Services credit at 28.3% YoY (83rd percentile, four-month rising streak) is the accelerant. The historical rhyme: the last time the CD ratio sustained above 80% during a rate pause, the system needed either a deposit rate war or macro-prudential tightening via risk weights. NBFC credit growth already moderating to 15.4% YoY from 15.8% suggests wholesale funding stress is arriving on schedule.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate is being compressed in real time: CPI just crossed 6%, making the ex-ante real rate negative. The RBI's data-dependent pause made sense at CPI 4.45% YoY two months ago; at 6.09% YoY, the same stance is a different decision. The second-order effect: a negative real rate with credit growing at 19.54% YoY is a deposit mobilisation problem — savers have no incentive to lock in term deposits, which is precisely why deposit growth is lagging. The RBI is not driving with one foot on the brake; it has both feet off the pedals.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (up from 16.1%) and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%) confirm the investment upcycle is broadening, not narrowing. Iron ore at $161.91/t — nearly double the prior month's $90.69/t — signals construction and steel demand is real, not statistical. The check: core sector at 4.8% YoY is decelerating, which means the capex signal from IIP is running ahead of the materials economy. Private capex typically accelerates above 80% capacity utilisation; at 77.4%, the incentive exists but the trigger hasn't been pulled.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹231290 cr/mo; PV 32.1% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,31,290 cr / month — 90th percentile — is the strongest collections print in recent memory, but the composition matters: a jump of this magnitude in a single month warrants scrutiny of advance filings and year-end adjustments before declaring a demand surge. Passenger vehicle sales at 32.1% YoY and two-wheeler at 33.1% YoY are unambiguously strong and span both urban discretionary and rural mass segments. The tension: e-commerce GMV growth at 25% YoY (up from 18%) confirms urban digital demand, but credit card growth at 2.3% YoY — the 23rd percentile — suggests the consumer is spending from income, not leverage. That is structurally healthy but limits the upside surprise.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.54% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 16.86% YoY — a 268 bps divergence widening for three consecutive months (13.8→17.1→19.4→19.54% credit; 10.8→17.8→16.86% deposits). CD ratio now 82% credit-to-deposits, up from 81% last month, at 75th percentile of 10-year range. Services credit surging 28.3% YoY (21.4→22.9→24.3→28.3%, three-month rising streak, 83rd percentile), while agriculture credit at 19.5% YoY (82nd percentile). NBFC credit growth moderating to 15.4% YoY from 15.8%, signalling wholesale funding stress.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% and deposit franchises in metros — they'll poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities; their cost of funds will spike. Watch for RBI to signal liquidity support via OMOs or CRR cuts within 6-8 weeks if CD ratio breaches 83%. Equity: buy PSU banks (deposit moat), sell mid-cap NBFCs with weak deposit bases.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile has historically preceded either RBI rate cuts (2020-21) or liquidity tightening (2022-23). The current divergence — credit accelerating while deposits decelerate — is a late-cycle signal that typically precedes either policy easing or credit rationing.","is_surprise":false}

signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Pullback","data_text":"Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (strong-negative signal -100, down from 2.81 mn sq ft / quarter, but recent data shows extreme volatility: 14.1→15.08→14.1→15.08→19.5→4.02, latest quarter is 79% below prior quarter). Office vacancy at 13.4% vacant (down from 14.5%, 37th percentile, improving). Rent in Bengaluru at ₹103.6/sqft/mo (61st percentile, down from ₹102.5, volatile: 109→163→103.6→168.8→168→103.6). Rent in Mumbai at ₹156/sqft/mo (60th percentile, up from ₹144.4, volatile: 178.7→156→135.8→342.6→343→156). IT credit growth at 19.5% YoY (76th percentile, rising 3 in a row: 19.2→20→18.2→19.5). Nifty IT index flat. US PMI composite at 58.4 (80th percentile, strong). Airline passenger traffic at 8.64 mn / month (strong-negative signal -100, down from 8.52 mn / month, but recent data shows collapse: 35.08→86.4→8.64, latest is 90% below prior quarter).","implication":"CROSS-DOMAIN INSIGHT: Office absorption collapsed 79% QoQ while IT credit growth remains at 76th percentile. This divergence signals that GCCs (Global Capability Centers) are the marginal buyer of office space, not traditional IT services. The collapse in absorption + flat Nifty IT suggests GCCs are consolidating footprints (fewer, larger centers) rather than expanding headcount. Airline traffic collapse (90% QoQ) is a data anomaly, but if real, it signals either a measurement error or a sudden travel shock. FALSIFIABLE: If GCC consolidation is real, we should see (1) office rents in Tier-1 cities (Mumbai, Bangalore) stabilizing or falling despite low vacancy, and (2) IT services companies reporting flat or negative headcount growth in India despite credit growth. ACTIONABLE: Underweight office REITs (Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield) — they're pricing in continued GCC expansion that isn't materializing. Overweight IT services with strong domestic cost arbitrage (TCS, Infosys) — they'll benefit from GCC consolidation (higher margins). Reduce exposure to commercial real estate developers betting on IT demand.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"Office absorption at -100 signal is a 10-year extreme; the 79% QoQ collapse is unprecedented in the dataset. This either signals a structural shift in GCC strategy (consolidation over expansion) or a data reporting anomaly. Historical precedent: 2020-21 saw similar office absorption volatility during COVID, but that was followed by a rebound. Current setup suggests structural, not cyclical, change.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP, 6.09% CPI — Growth and Inflation Now Collide

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY, PMI Composite at 56.5, and IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY signal broad expansion across manufacturing and investment.
  • But CPI at 6.09% YoY has crossed the RBI's 6% ceiling — food inflation at 8.94% YoY and fuel at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) are the drivers.
  • Core CPI at 4.5% YoY is rising but secondary; the supply-side shocks in food and fuel are what rate policy cannot easily address.
  • GST at ₹2,31,290 cr / month (90th percentile) and PV sales at 32.1% YoY confirm demand is not the inflation source — making the RBI's dilemma structural, not cyclical.

The tension: Growth is accelerating and inflation is simultaneously breaching the tolerance band — the RBI's pause, calibrated for a 4–5% CPI world, is now operating in a 6% world with a negative real repo rate.

Bottom line: Watch whether RBI's next communiqué upgrades the inflation forecast above 5.1% YoY — any revision signals the pause is over and rate normalisation is back on the table.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US Re-accelerates, BOJ Tightens — The Carry Trade Unwinds

The facts:

  • US GDP SAAR at 4.3% SAAR (four-quarter rising streak) and PMI Composite at 58.4 (80th percentile) signal genuine re-acceleration, not a survey artefact.
  • But US 10Y Treasury at 4.85% yield (88th percentile) has fallen for five consecutive months even as the Fed funds rate rose to 3.88% p.a. — the bond market is not pricing the growth story.
  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. — a 10-year high, 100th percentile — is the underappreciated tail: every 25 bps of BOJ tightening unwinds yen-funded carry trades that have been long EM assets.
  • China PMI Composite at 49.5 (contraction) prevents any commodity reflation from sustaining — Brent at $90.84/bbl has a ceiling, not a floor.

The tension: DM surveys price re-acceleration; bond markets and China price deceleration. The BOJ is the variable neither side has fully priced — its tightening cycle is the fastest in four decades and the yen carry unwind has direct transmission to India FII flows.

Bottom line: BOJ's next meeting is the single most important external event for India liquidity; a further 25 bps hike would accelerate FII outflows beyond the current -₹4,516 cr / month.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP Plateau Meets FII Retreat — DII Absorption Fading

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,160 cr / month (94th percentile) remain elevated in level but YoY growth has decelerated to 8.9% YoY (28th percentile) — the retail bid is plateauing.
  • Equity MF net inflows fell to ₹32,994 cr net / month from ₹38,307 cr net / month prior month — the marginal domestic buyer is pulling back.
  • FII equity net at -₹4,516 cr net / month and DII equity net at ₹6,222 cr net / month (35th percentile, down from ₹51,829 cr net / month two months prior) — the DII cushion that absorbed the ₹49,935 cr FII exodus is no longer available at that scale.
  • But MF AUM at ₹83.39 lakh cr (86th percentile) and SIP AUM at ₹17.68 lakh cr (91st percentile) mean the stock of domestic capital is large — the flow is the concern, not the stock.

The tension: The market has been absorbing FII outflows via DII flows; DII flows are now compressing toward their 35th-percentile run rate precisely as BOJ tightening threatens to extend FII selling.

Bottom line: If DII equity net falls below ₹5,000 cr / month for two consecutive months while FII remains negative, Nifty's 86th-percentile valuation has no domestic backstop.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

REITs Price GCC Risk; Residential Splits Between Hyderabad and Chennai

The facts:

  • NRI buying is FALLING — NRI share of residential purchases at 18% (down 2 pp), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 32%; remittances at $155.1 bn (14.5% YoY) provide macro support but the transaction share is declining.
  • Hyderabad leads residential momentum: sales +15% YoY, launches +120% YoY, only 28 months unsold inventory — but the launch surge risks oversupply within 6 quarters.
  • Office absorption collapsed to 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter from 19.5 mn sq ft / quarter prior — a single-quarter drop of 79% — with GCCs at 42% of occupier mix most exposed to US tech spending decisions.
  • Embassy REIT at ₹369.92/unit, Mindspace at ₹345.06/unit, Brookfield at ₹263.49/unit — all down 13–31% from prior prints — are pricing the office absorption collapse before the equity market has.

The tension: Residential demand in Hyderabad and Bengaluru is real; office demand has fallen off a cliff in a single quarter. REITs are the honest signal — the equity market's Nifty at 86th percentile has not yet processed what the REIT market already has.

Bottom line: Avoid office REITs until GCC hiring data from US tech firms confirms a re-acceleration; overweight residential developers with Hyderabad and Bengaluru exposure over MMR and NCR.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Risks, One Trigger — BOJ Pulls the Thread

The facts:

  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, rising) — yen carry unwind accelerates FII outflows and INR depreciation; probability high, impact severe.
  • CPI at 6.09% YoY breaching the RBI ceiling forces a policy reversal — repo hike would compress NIM, reprice mortgages, and stall the capex cycle; probability medium-high.
  • CD ratio at 82% with services credit at 28.3% YoY — if deposit growth slips below 15% YoY, RBI risk-weight action on unsecured lending becomes probable within two quarters.
  • But office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (79% below prior quarter) — if GCC demand does not recover by Q1 2027, REIT distributions face cuts and the commercial real estate credit book deteriorates.

The tension: All four risks share a common transmission: a BOJ hike triggers INR weakness, which forces RBI's hand on rates, which tightens the CD ratio further, which hits NBFC funding — the chain is sequential, not independent.

Bottom line: Watch the BOJ policy meeting: a rate hold keeps the chain intact; a 25 bps hike to 1.50% p.a. activates all four risks simultaneously within 60 days.

"}
